summary: One screen in a multi-step onboarding flow, like a welcome tour with next/back navigation.
description: MultiStageProtonScreen (function component) and ProtonScreen (React.PureComponent it renders) implement one step of the multi-screen stepper-style onboarding flow used by about:welcome, Spotlight, and FeatureCallout tours — rendering the step-progress indicator (StepsIndicator or ProgressBar), title/subtitle, hero image/tiles, and action buttons for the current screen's content config. A real React implementation, not a custom element.

attributes.name: content
attributes.description: Required per-screen config, read directly in ProtonScreen.render(): title, subtitle, position ("center"|"split"|"callout"|...), background/background_static, hero_image, tiles, primary_button/secondary_button/additional_button, dismiss_button, checkbox, progress_bar, steps_indicator, logo, narrow, fullscreen, zap_border, zap_shadow, video_container, cta_paragraph, info_text, languageSwitcher, and more.

attributes.name: id
attributes.description: Screen id, used as a CSS class on the rendered <main>.

attributes.name: order
attributes.description: Zero-based index of this screen; used for the steps indicator's current-step count and to alternate the screen-1/screen-2 background class.

attributes.name: totalNumberOfScreens
attributes.description: Total screen count, used by the steps indicator.

attributes.name: previousOrder
attributes.description: Order of the previously shown screen; used for step-transition numbering and to detect the very first screen shown.

attributes.name: handleAction
attributes.description: Callback invoked by buttons/checkbox/tiles with a synthetic event-like object carrying a `value` naming which content-tree action to take.

attributes.name: navigate
attributes.description: Advances or dismisses the tour; called directly by MultiStageProtonScreen's own auto-advance effect.

attributes.name: autoAdvance
attributes.description: Optional; when set, MultiStageProtonScreen calls handleAction automatically after a timeout (autoAdvance.actionTimeMS, default 20000ms).

attributes.name: advanceOnExperimentLoad
attributes.description: Optional; alternative to autoAdvance — waits for window.AWWaitForNimbus() (bounded by minDisplayMs/maxDisplayMs) then calls navigate(false).

attributes.name: isFirstScreen
attributes.description: Affects the dialog-initial CSS class.

attributes.name: isLastScreen
attributes.description: Affects the dialog-last CSS class.

attributes.name: isSingleScreen
attributes.description: When true, hides the steps indicator.

attributes.name: requireAction
attributes.description: When true, focuses the title heading on mount instead of the main content container, and makes the title focusable.

attributes.name: ariaRole
attributes.description: Role for the rendered <main>; defaults to "alertdialog".

attributes.name: forceHideStepsIndicator
attributes.description: Forces the steps indicator to be hidden regardless of other conditions.

attributes.name: aboveButtonStepsIndicator
attributes.description: Renders the steps indicator above the action buttons instead of at the end of main content.

attributes.name: animationsPaused
attributes.description: Swaps animated background/hero-image assets for their _static counterparts, and reflects a pressed play/pause toggle.

attributes.name: toggleAnimationsPaused
attributes.description: Callback for the animation play/pause button.

attributes.name: isRtamo, addonId, addonType, addonName, addonURL, addonIconURL, themeScreenshots, installedAddons
attributes.description: Props for the 'return to AMO' addon-install flow, used to render an install button/icon in place of the normal primary action.

attributes.name: messageId
attributes.description: Destructured directly in the MultiStageProtonScreen function component's own top-level props (separately from the content-config props it forwards to ProtonScreen).

attributes.name: isWideScreen
attributes.description: Read in ProtonScreen.render(); affects layout for wide-viewport presentations.

usage:
<MultiStageProtonScreen
  content={screenContent}
  id={screenContent.id}
  order={order}
  totalNumberOfScreens={screens.length}
  handleAction={handleAction}
  navigate={navigate}
/>
